operating_notes.text: The fifth amusement park at Chennai commenced commercial operations with effect from 2 December 2025.
QIP of ₹540 Cr (issue period December 03, 2024 to December 06, 2024) was fully utilised by March 31, 2026; ₹39 Cr was reallocated from the Chennai park to general corporate purposes in Q4FY26.
Q4FY26 park-wise footfalls: Bengaluru 2.19 lakh, Kochi 2.14 lakh, Hyderabad 2.09 lakh, Bhubaneshwar 0.46 lakh, Chennai 1.91 lakh.
FY26 park-wise footfalls: Bengaluru 10.46 lakh, Kochi 8.48 lakh, Hyderabad 8.68 lakh, Bhubaneshwar 1.91 lakh, Chennai 2.66 lakh.
Isle by Wonderla resort in Bangalore commenced operations from 9 May 2025.
Chennai park ran at 30% EBITDA margin in Q4FY26, in line with mature Kochi and Hyderabad parks.
Non-ticket revenue is 30% of the mix versus 70% ticket revenue; management targets 50-50 in 4-5 years.
Capital work in progress of ₹102.9 Cr relates to Chennai Sky Wheel and new rides, to be capitalised in Q1FY27.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (standalone): revenue ₹135.85 Cr (+40.4% YoY), net profit ₹16.42 Cr (+49.1% YoY).
Wonderla Holidays reappointed Deloitte Haskins & Sells as statutory auditors for a five-year term on 7 May 2026.
Wonderla Holidays Limited’s Board of Directors, led by **Srinivasulu Raju Yellamraju**, recommended a final dividend of ₹2 per equity share (20% of ₹10 face value) on May 7, 2026.
Wonderla Holidays released its monitoring agency report for Q4FY26 confirming full utilization of ₹540 Cr QIP proceeds.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): total income ₹142.05 Cr (+32% YoY), EBITDA ₹50.01 Cr (+64%), PAT ₹16.42 Cr (+49%); FY26 PAT ₹81.73 Cr (-25% on prior-year deferred tax credit).

Wonderla Holidays Limited hosted an earnings conference call on November 7, 2025, discussing Q4FY26 performance with investors/analysts, with audio recording available at https://www.wonderla.com/investor-relations/communication-and-disclosures.

Wonderla's Q4FY26 call on 8 May 2026 guided FY27 sustaining capex of ₹35-40 Cr with no large new park, said Chennai ran at 30% EBITDA margin, and flagged talks with at least four state governments for new sites.

Arun K Chittilappilly, Chittilappilly Thomas Kochouseph, Sheela Grace Kochouseph, Kochouseph Thomas Chittilappilly, Kochouseph Chittilappilly, and Priya Sarah Cheeran Joseph declared no encumbrance on their shares in Wonderla Holidays Limited for FY2026.
